design: 181 of 1211 asks (15%), stratified by theme in proportion to the population (at least one per theme), then shuffled; review in order so any completed prefix is random.

themes.label: Data provenance, traceability & quality assurance
themes.definition: Documenting where data came from and how they were transformed (lineage, ETL, curation), and the QA/QC plans, data-quality checks and metrics that demonstrate reliability.
themes.notes: Includes: provenance, traceability, audit trails of transformations, data-quality metrics/thresholds, QA/QC templates. Excludes: who holds/gives access to data (T06); validation of specific study variables (T03).

themes.label: Data relevance, fit for purpose & representativeness
themes.definition: Whether a data source suits the study question: capture of the population, exposures and outcomes; health-system context; EHR-vs-claims differences; representativeness of populations, including health-equity and SDOH concerns.
themes.notes: Includes: health-system background/formulary information requests, continuity/observability, EHR vs claims specific considerations, diversity/representativeness. Excludes: missing-data methods (T04).

themes.label: Methodology: validation, study design & analytic methods
themes.definition: How study variables are defined and validated (algorithms, PPV/sensitivity/specificity, chart review, reference standards, reuse of prior validation) and how studies are designed and analysed (time periods/index dates, comparators, estimands and target-trial framing, prespecification and registration, feasibility exploration before analysis, confounding, quantitative bias analysis).
themes.notes: Includes: performance thresholds, validation sample size, no gold standard, QBA, immortal time, negative controls, protocol/SAP timing. Excludes: complaints that validation is too burdensome in general (T07) unless the ask is about the method itself.

themes.label: Missing data & data completeness
themes.definition: Definition, characterisation and handling of missing, absent or unavailable data, including mortality capture and loss to follow-up.
themes.notes: Includes: missing vs absent framing, imputation, proxies, death data/NDI access. Excludes: alignment of the missing-data definition with ICH E9(R1) when the ask is purely about alignment (T09).

themes.label: Linkage & tokenization
themes.definition: Methods and documentation for linking data sources: deterministic vs probabilistic linkage, tokenization, linkage quality, and selection bias in linked cohorts.
themes.notes: Includes: linkage error, hashing/MPI transparency. Excludes: privacy as such (T11) unless the ask is about the linkage method.

themes.label: Data access, roles of data holders, retention & auditability
themes.definition: What sponsors can obtain from data vendors/holders, the split of responsibilities between sponsors and data providers, proprietary algorithms/IP, FDA access to patient-level data, retention and inspection.
themes.notes: Includes: licence limits, vendor vs sponsor accountability, submission of datasets/programs, retention periods. Excludes: provenance documentation content (T01).

themes.label: Proportionality, sponsor burden & feasibility
themes.definition: Asks that recommendations be risk-based, tiered by regulatory use, or relaxed because they are infeasible or exceed what is required of RCTs.
themes.notes: Includes: risk-based validation, 'unprecedented hurdles', infeasible documentation. Excludes: asks that only want more detail on a requirement (code to its topic).

themes.label: Terminology & definitional clarity
themes.definition: Requests to define, rename or clarify terms and concepts used in the guidance.
themes.notes: Includes: continuity of care vs coverage, data lineage, verification vs validation as terms, glossary edits. Excludes: substantive requests that happen to use a term.

themes.label: Alignment with other guidance & data standards
themes.definition: Consistency with ICH (esp. E9(R1)), other FDA RWE guidances, HHS/ONC policy and data standards (USCDI, FHIR, CDISC, OMOP), and international bodies.
themes.notes: Includes: harmonise definitions with ICH E9(R1), retire/merge the 2013 guidance, STaRT-RWE, adopt FHIR/common data models. EMA/international alignment was rarely raised.

themes.label: FDA engagement & implementation support
themes.definition: How sponsors and data providers interact with FDA (meetings, protocol review, timelines) and tools FDA could provide: examples, case studies, templates, checklists, workshops, phenotype libraries.
themes.notes: Includes: meeting pathways, publication of precedents, regulatory-grade phenotype library. Excludes: study registration (T13).

themes.label: Privacy & data governance
themes.definition: Patient privacy, consent, de-identification and re-identification risk, HIPAA and governance frameworks.
themes.notes: Includes: privacy-preserving linkage when the ask is privacy-motivated, consent processes. Excludes: data access licences (T06).

themes.label: Scope & data types
themes.definition: What the guidance covers or should cover: product types, data types (pharmacy claims, registries, unstructured data/NLP, genomics, PROs, non-US data, clearinghouses), uses (external controls) and the overall role of RWE.
themes.notes: Includes: expand/limit scope, acceptability of NLP/AI-derived variables as a data type, statements that RWE should only be supplementary. Excludes: validation of an NLP variable (T03).
